drug_class: SGLT2 inhibitor combined with a biguanide antidiabetic
purpose: This medication is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines two different medicines into one pill to make it easier to manage your diabetes. It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range.
how_it_works: Ertugliflozin works by telling your kidneys to remove extra sugar from your blood and pass it out through your urine, so your blood sugar levels go down. Metformin works by reducing the amount of sugar your liver makes and helping your body use insulin more effectively. Together, these two medicines work in different ways to keep your blood sugar under better control.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include urinary tract infections, yeast infections in the genital area, upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and low blood sugar especially if you take other diabetes medicines. Some people also notice they urinate more often than usual.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have kidney problems, liver problems, or a condition called diabetic ketoacidosis. It can rarely cause a serious but uncommon condition called lactic acidosis from the metformin component, so tell your doctor right away if you feel very weak, have unusual muscle pain, or have trouble breathing. Stop taking it before any surgery or procedure using contrast dye. It may also increase the risk of a rare but serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene — seek medical help immediately if you have pain, redness, or swelling in the genital or rectal area.
typical_dosing: This medicine is usually taken twice a day with meals to help reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will choose the right strength based on your current medications and kidney function. Never crush or split the tablet — swallow it whole. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
